result.title: KVPath: Connecting Key-Value Representations Across Transformer Layers
result.summary: Transformers typically cache an independent key-value (KV) representation for each token at every layer. Recent work reveals that a token's KV representations across neighboring layers are correlated and contain shared information. We hypothesize that this correlation implies incremental inter-layer changes, which can be effectively captured by low-dimensional deltas. Motivated by this, we propose KVPath, a new KV representation paradigm that connects KV representations across the network depth into a path. The path establishes a full-dimensional base KV at the first layer, while subsequent layers generate low-dimensional delta KVs to update the preceding KV, thereby constructing their own KV states. By caching the base KV once alongside these compact delta KVs, KVPath preserves distinct layer-specific representations without storing full KV states at every layer. We develop two variants of KVPath: KVPath-Residual, which updates vector values via residual addition, and KVPath-Rolling, which progressively updates feature dimensions in a rolling manner. Under matched parameter counts, KVPath reduces KV-cache storage by up to 68\% for Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and 55\% for Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), while maintaining or even improving model performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 KVPath，把各层 KV 表示串成一条路径：首层存全维 base KV，后续层只生成低维 delta 增量更新前一层状态，并给出残差加法与滚动维度更新两个变体，在 GQA 与 MLA 下显著压缩 KV-cache。
AI.relevance_reason: 「低维增量承载跨层状态变化」的机制可能为 LVR 中跨深度或跨推理步的 latent 状态压缩与增量更新提供借鉴，也与 KV 缓存和注意力结构影响 latent 相似度的关注点相关；但原文面向推理效率，未涉及视觉证据或多模态推理，迁移可行性需核查。
